SAMPADA data put the prevalence of anaemia at 31% in children between 5-9 years, 46% among adolescent girls, 55% among adult women up to the age of 59 years, 56% in women above 60 years, and 58% among lactating women. File photograph used for representational purposes only | Photo Credit: DEEPAK KR
Data put out by the Ministry of health and Family Welfare as per the latest SAMPADA (Survey for Assessment of Markers of Population Health, Activity, Diet and Anthropometry), claims a drop in prevalence of anaemia levels across age and gender groups. Among children, it has dropped to 41.8 %, as against the previous figure from National Family Health Survey-5 data of 64%; among women it has dropped to 56% from 57%, and in pregnant women, the current survey puts it at 44% (down from 52%). Among men, SAMPADA says, anaemia has dropped to 19% (from 25% in NFHS-5).
